content: At the beginning of the Expert Group meeting, the co-chair, Karin Weyer from the Stop TB Department, summarized the declarations of interest (DOI) statements. The meeting was held in the context of the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, specifically focusing on tests for tuberculosis infection. Two individuals, P. Hill and R. O’Brien, declared conflicts of interest that were considered insignificant. P. Hill disclosed receiving kits from Cellestis (now QIAGEN) and Oxford Immunotec for research purposes. R. O’Brien reported receiving support from the Foundation for Innovative New Diagnostics (FIND) for academic projects, including the development of a point-of-care serodiagnostic test and the FIND biomarker discovery project. Certain individuals with intellectual or research involvement in the use of interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in lowand middle-income settings were invited as observers. Their role was to provide technical input and address technical questions. For example, P. Godfrey-Fausett disclosed receiving a research grant to investigate the use of the QuantiFERON-TB Gold In-Tube assay in South Africa and Zambia. M. Pai reported conducting research studies on IGRAs. These individuals did not participate in the GRADE evaluation process and were excluded from the Expert Group discussions when recommendations were being developed. They also did not contribute to the final Expert Group meeting report, the preparation of the Strategic and Technical Advisory Group for Tuberculosis (STAG-TB) documentation, or the final WHO policy statement. The systematic reviewers (A. Cattamanchi, A. Date, A. Detjen, D. Dowdy, R. Menzies, J. Metcalfe, M. Pai, M. Rangaka, K. Steingart, and A. Zwerling) were also deemed to have conflicts of interest. As a result, they participated in the meeting only as observers, providing technical clarifications on the findings of the systematic reviews. They did not take part in the GRADE evaluation process, the discussions where recommendations were developed, or the preparation of the final WHO policy statement. References for Annex 3 include the WHO website on declarations of interest, the second edition of the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development, and several published articles addressing challenges and opportunities in tuberculosis prevention and treatment in low-income and middle-income countries. These references provide additional context and evidence for the discussions and recommendations made during the meeting.
